label: 七塔灰光
parentStaticReview: Parent accepted the corrected quartet on 2026-10-20 after one bounded imagegen-only short-rays stone-tone correction. Minor remaining lighting variation is disclosed.
actualCaveats: The fan expands from three rays to seven, grows to the crest, then returns to three thinner rays. This is an energy-envelope change, not seven conserved solid objects translating through space.
Total alpha mass changes by about +27.0%, +42.9%, then -47.0%. The crest-to-residual change can feel abrupt at 12 fps. It is authored geometry loss rather than a global opacity fade.

Six airborne stones appear at rising-fan and move outward/upward at the crest. The two high stones retire by the final pose; four lower stones settle, with the small left stone contacting the rubble contour. Three final stones remain separate alpha128 components. No full landing or unique particle correspondence is claimed.

The selected short-rays tone repair reduces the whole lower-tower mean luminance from 81.55 to 65.19 versus crest 60.90. The other selected poses measure 63.67 and 62.55. Minor material-lighting and amber-core variation remains, although the severe initial light-stone jump is removed.
Tower bounds vary at most 2 source pixels (0.045 logical pixels) and fixed material ROI best offsets are at most 1 pixel per axis. Source shading and exact ray edges are not byte-identical.
The original peak central ray is clipped by the atlas crop. The new peak has a complete visible tip at y65 with genuine exterior margins; the correction is intentional, not a matching failure.
Tiny floating fragments and dark tower details are subordinate at 32 pixels, especially on black/dark earth, and clearer at 64 pixels. Live browser/game playback remains unobserved.
The last frame is a nonblank terminal pose. No 4-to-1 seam, blank ending, scene removal time or 420 ms lifetime is inferred for this catalog-only nonloop effect.
diagnosticTiming: Separate slow-diagnostic-repeat APNGs use 3 fps with infinite repetition, not the runtime contract.
browserReason: Known blocked browser/GPU environment; no repeated escalation. Only encoding, decoded frame identity and static phase review are verified.
